en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} habló a Moisés. Le dijo:
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés:

sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alizungumza na Musa. Akamwambia,
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa,

decisions.choice: the last instructions given at Sinai before Israel leaves
decisions.reason: Chapter 9 ended with the cloud that tells Israel when to camp and when to move (9:15-23). This speech adds the trumpets that pass those signals on to the whole people, and from verse 11 the march from Sinai begins.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("parla", "partirent"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit", "sont partis"); the instructions of verses 2-10 in the future or present at Literal and Balanced ("vous sonnerez"), the imperative or "vous devez" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for each passage with narration: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of the plain Readable level. Verses 2-10 are the LORD's instructions and take the forms used for commands.

source.text: עֲשֵׂ֣ה לְךָ֗ שְׁתֵּי֙ חֲצֽוֹצְרֹ֣ת כֶּ֔סֶף מִקְשָׁ֖ה תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑ם וְהָי֤וּ לְךָ֙ לְמִקְרָ֣א הָֽעֵדָ֔ה וּלְמַסַּ֖ע אֶת־הַֽמַּחֲנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Make for yourself two trumpets of silver; hammered work you will make them, and they will be for you for summoning the congregation and for setting out the camps.

en.L: "Make for yourself two trumpets of silver; you shall make them of hammered work. And they shall be for you for summoning the congregation and for setting out the camps.
en.B: "Make two trumpets of hammered silver. You are to use them to call the congregation together and to set the camps moving.
en.R: "Make two trumpets out of hammered silver. Use them to call the community together and to tell the camps when to move.

es.L: «Hazte dos trompetas de plata; de obra labrada a martillo las harás. Y te serán para convocar a la comunidad y para la partida de los campamentos.
es.B: «Haz dos trompetas de plata labrada a martillo. Las usarás para reunir a la comunidad y para poner en marcha los campamentos.
es.R: «Haz dos trompetas de plata labrada a martillo. Úsalas para reunir a la comunidad y para avisar a los campamentos cuándo deben ponerse en marcha.

fr.L: « Fais-toi deux trompettes d’argent ; tu les feras en travail martelé. Et elles seront pour toi pour convoquer la communauté et pour le départ des camps.
fr.B: « Fais deux trompettes d’argent martelé. Tu t’en serviras pour rassembler la communauté et pour mettre les camps en marche.
fr.R: « Fabrique deux trompettes en argent martelé. Utilise-les pour réunir la communauté et pour dire aux camps quand partir.

sw.L: "Jifanyie tarumbeta mbili za fedha; utazifanya kwa kazi ya kufua. Nazo zitakuwa kwako kwa kuiita jumuiya na kwa kuzisafirisha kambi.
sw.B: "Tengeneza tarumbeta mbili za fedha iliyofuliwa. Utazitumia kuikusanya jumuiya na kuziondoa kambi zianze safari.
sw.R: "Tengeneza tarumbeta mbili kwa fedha iliyofuliwa. Zitumie kuiita jumuiya ikusanyike na kuziambia kambi wakati wa kuondoka.

decisions.choice: trumpets: straight metal trumpets, not the ram's horn
decisions.reason: This word names a long, straight trumpet of metal, different from the ram's horn (shofar) blown at Sinai (Exodus 19:16, 19). Silver trumpets of this kind are blown by priests elsewhere too (1 Chronicles 15:24; 2 Chronicles 5:12).

decisions.choice: hammered work: beaten into shape from silver, not cast in a mold
decisions.reason: The same word describes the gold cherubim and the lampstand, each beaten out of a single piece (Exodus 25:18, 31, 36).

decisions.choice: setting out the camps: breaking camp to move on
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb for pulling up tent pegs and moving on. The trumpets have two uses: to call the people together (verses 3-4, 7) and to start the march (verses 5-6).

decisions.choice: leaves out "for yourself" and "for you"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "for yourself" marks the trumpets as Moses' to make and use; Balanced and Readable say this with "make" and "use" addressed to him. Literal keeps both phrases.

decisions.choice: "trompetas"
decisions.reason: The word names a long, straight metal trumpet; "trompeta" is that instrument, kept apart from "el cuerno de carnero" (the shofar of Exodus 19).

decisions.choice: "trompettes"
decisions.reason: The word names a long, straight metal trumpet. French "trompette" is that instrument; the ram's horn of Exodus 19 is "la corne de bélier", so the two stay apart as in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "tarumbeta"
decisions.reason: The word names a long, straight metal trumpet. "Tarumbeta" is that instrument; "baragumu" is a horn and would blur the difference from the ram's horn (pembe ya kondoo dume) of Exodus 19.

source.text: וְתָקְע֖וּ בָּהֵ֑ן וְנֽוֹעֲד֤וּ אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will blow on them, and will gather to you all the congregation at [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.

en.L: And when they blow on them, all the congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.B: When they blow both trumpets, all the congregation must come together before you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.R: When the priests blow both trumpets, the whole community must come to you at the entrance of the meeting tent.

es.L: Y cuando las toquen, toda la comunidad se reunirá contigo a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro.
es.B: Cuando se toquen las dos trompetas, toda la comunidad deberá reunirse ante ti a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro.
es.R: Cuando los sacerdotes toquen las dos trompetas, toda la comunidad debe venir a ti a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro.

fr.L: Et quand ils en sonneront, toute la communauté se rassemblera auprès de toi à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre.
fr.B: Quand on sonnera des deux trompettes, toute la communauté devra se réunir devant toi à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre.
fr.R: Quand les prêtres sonneront des deux trompettes, toute la communauté doit venir vers toi à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre.

sw.L: Nao watakapozipiga, jumuiya yote itakusanyika kwako mlangoni pa Hema la Kukutania.
sw.B: Tarumbeta zote mbili zitakapopigwa, jumuiya yote itakusanyika mbele yako kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania.
sw.R: Makuhani watakapopiga tarumbeta zote mbili, lazima jumuiya yote ije kwako kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania.

decisions.choice: they blow on them: both trumpets are blown
decisions.reason: "Them" is the two trumpets, and verse 4 sets it against blowing "on one". A blast on both calls the whole people; a blast on one calls only the leaders.

decisions.choice: they: the priests who blow the trumpets
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject here. Verse 8 says who blows: the sons of Aaron, the priests.

decisions.choice: they blow both trumpets
decisions.reason: Balanced says "both" to make the contrast with verse 4 plain.

decisions.choice: the priests blow both trumpets
decisions.reason: Readable names the priests from verse 8 as the ones who blow, and says "both" for the contrast with verse 4.

decisions.choice: "sonner de" the trumpets ("ils en sonneront", "sonner des deux trompettes")
decisions.reason: This is the plain blast of verses 3-4 and 7. "Sonner de la trompette" is the usual French for playing a trumpet signal and keeps "sonner l'alarme" (verse 5) as its contrast.

decisions.choice: "kupiga" tarumbeta
decisions.reason: "Kupiga tarumbeta" is the ordinary Swahili for sounding a trumpet; the alarm of verse 5 is "kupiga mlio wa hatari", so the same verb carries both signals as in the Hebrew.

source.text: וְאִם־בְּאַחַ֖ת יִתְקָ֑עוּ וְנוֹעֲד֤וּ אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ הַנְּשִׂיאִ֔ים רָאשֵׁ֖י אַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And if on one they blow, and will gather to you the leaders, [the] heads of [the] thousands of Israel.

en.L: But if they blow on one, then the leaders, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather to you.
en.B: When a single trumpet is blown, the leaders, who head Israel's clans, are to come to you.
en.R: If they blow only one trumpet, then only the leaders must come to you. These are the men who head Israel's clans.

es.L: Pero si tocan una sola, se reunirán contigo los jefes, las cabezas de los millares de Israel.
es.B: Cuando se toque una sola trompeta, los jefes, que encabezan los clanes de Israel, vendrán a ti.
es.R: Si tocan solo una trompeta, solo los jefes deben venir a ti. Son los hombres que dirigen los clanes de Israel.

fr.L: Mais si l’on sonne d’une seule, alors les chefs, ceux qui sont à la tête des milliers d’Israël, se rassembleront auprès de toi.
fr.B: Quand on ne sonnera que d’une seule trompette, ce sont les chefs, qui dirigent les clans d’Israël, qui viendront à toi.
fr.R: Si l’on sonne d’une seule trompette, seuls les chefs doivent venir vers toi. Ce sont les hommes qui dirigent les clans d’Israël.

sw.L: Lakini wakipiga moja, ndipo viongozi, wakuu wa maelfu ya Israeli, watakusanyika kwako.
sw.B: Tarumbeta moja tu ikipigwa, viongozi, walio wakuu wa koo za Israeli, watakuja kwako.
sw.R: Wakipiga tarumbeta moja tu, lazima viongozi peke yao waje kwako. Hao ndio wanaume wanaoongoza koo za Israeli.

decisions.choice: the thousands of Israel: the large divisions of the people
decisions.reason: The word means "thousand", and it also names a large unit of the people, a clan grouping or a military unit (1:16; Exodus 18:21, 25). Here it names the groups whose heads the leaders are, not an exact count. See the note on the size of the census numbers in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: the leaders, the heads: the men named in 1:5-16
decisions.reason: The leaders of the twelve tribes were listed in 1:5-16, where they are also called "heads of the thousands of Israel" (1:16). The same men lead their tribes in the march below (verses 14-27).

decisions.choice: clans
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "clans" for the groups these men led, as in 1:16, since "heads of the thousands" would read as heads of numbers. ("Divisions" is kept for the army units of chapter 2.) Literal keeps "thousands".

decisions.choice: only the leaders ... These are the men who head
decisions.reason: Readable adds "only" to bring out the contrast with verse 3, and splits the title into its own sentence.

source.text: וּתְקַעְתֶּ֖ם תְּרוּעָ֑ה וְנָֽסְעוּ֙ הַֽמַּחֲנ֔וֹת הַחֹנִ֖ים קֵֽדְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will blow an alarm, and will set out the camps camping eastward.

en.L: And when you blow an alarm, the camps that camp on the east side shall set out.
en.B: When you sound the alarm signal, the camps on the east side are to set out.
en.R: When you blow the loud call, the camps on the east side must start moving.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:toquen|toquéis}} alarma, partirán los campamentos que acampan al oriente.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:den|deis}} el toque de alarma, partirán los campamentos del lado oriental.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:den|deis}} el toque fuerte, los campamentos del lado este deben ponerse en marcha.

fr.L: Et quand vous sonnerez l’alarme, les camps qui campent à l’est partiront.
fr.B: Quand vous sonnerez le signal d’alarme, les camps situés du côté est partiront.
fr.R: Quand vous sonnerez le grand signal, les camps du côté est doivent se mettre en marche.

sw.L: Nanyi mtakapopiga mlio wa hatari, kambi zilizopiga kambi upande wa mashariki zitasafiri.
sw.B: Mtakapopiga mlio wa tahadhari, kambi zilizo upande wa mashariki zitaanza safari.
sw.R: Mtakapopiga mlio mkubwa, lazima kambi za upande wa mashariki zianze kuondoka.

decisions.choice: an alarm: a loud, rising signal blast, different from a plain blast
decisions.reason: The text uses two kinds of sound. The verb in verses 3-4 means a blast on the trumpet; the noun here names a loud signal or shout, the sound of a call to march or to battle (verse 9; Joshua 6:5, 20). Verse 7 keeps them apart: the plain blast gathers the assembly, the alarm sets the camps moving. The exact difference in sound is not described.

decisions.choice: the camps on the east: Judah, Issachar and Zebulun
decisions.reason: Chapter 2 placed the tribes in four camps of three around the tabernacle. Judah's camp was on the east, the side of the entrance (2:3-9), and it marched first (verse 14).

decisions.choice: alarm (Literal); the alarm signal (Balanced); the loud call (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "alarm" for this word through the chapter. Balanced adds "signal", since here the sound starts a march, not a warning of danger. Readable uses "loud call" to keep it apart from the plain blast.

decisions.choice: "alarma" (L); "el toque de alarma" (B); "el toque fuerte" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps one word for the alarm through the chapter; Balanced calls it a trumpet "toque", a signal; Readable says "el toque fuerte" to keep it apart from the plain blast ("tocar"). In war (verse 9) every level says "alarma".

decisions.choice: "l'alarme" (L); "le signal d'alarme" (B); "le grand signal" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps one word for the alarm through the chapter; Balanced adds "signal", since here it starts a march; Readable says "le grand signal" to keep it apart from the plain blast ("sonner des trompettes"). In war (verse 9) every level says "l'alarme".

decisions.choice: "mlio wa hatari" (L); "mlio wa tahadhari" (B); "mlio mkubwa" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mlio wa hatari" (alarm call) through the chapter; Balanced says "tahadhari" (alert), since here the call starts a march, not a warning of danger; Readable says "mlio mkubwa" (loud call), as the English. In war (verse 9) every level says "mlio wa hatari".

source.text: וּתְקַעְתֶּ֤ם תְּרוּעָה֙ שֵׁנִ֔ית וְנָֽסְעוּ֙ הַֽמַּחֲנ֔וֹת הַחֹנִ֖ים תֵּימָ֑נָה תְּרוּעָ֥ה יִתְקְע֖וּ לְמַסְעֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will blow an alarm a second [time], and will set out the camps camping southward; an alarm they will blow for their settings out.

en.L: And when you blow an alarm a second time, the camps that camp on the south side shall set out. They shall blow an alarm for their setting out.
en.B: When you sound the alarm signal a second time, the camps on the south side are to set out. The alarm signal is to be sounded whenever they set out.
en.R: When you blow the loud call a second time, the camps on the south side must start moving. The loud call is the signal for the camps to move.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:toquen|toquéis}} alarma por segunda vez, partirán los campamentos que acampan al sur. Tocarán alarma para sus partidas.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:den|deis}} el toque de alarma por segunda vez, partirán los campamentos del lado sur. El toque de alarma se dará siempre que tengan que partir.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:den|deis}} el toque fuerte por segunda vez, los campamentos del lado sur deben ponerse en marcha. El toque fuerte es la señal para que los campamentos partan.

fr.L: Et quand vous sonnerez l’alarme une deuxième fois, les camps qui campent au sud partiront. On sonnera l’alarme pour leurs départs.
fr.B: Quand vous sonnerez le signal d’alarme une deuxième fois, les camps situés du côté sud partiront. On sonnera le signal d’alarme chaque fois qu’ils devront partir.
fr.R: Quand vous sonnerez le grand signal une deuxième fois, les camps du côté sud doivent se mettre en marche. Le grand signal est celui qui dit aux camps de partir.

sw.L: Na mtakapopiga mlio wa hatari mara ya pili, kambi zilizopiga kambi upande wa kusini zitasafiri. Watapiga mlio wa hatari kwa safari zao.
sw.B: Mtakapopiga mlio wa tahadhari mara ya pili, kambi zilizo upande wa kusini zitaanza safari. Mlio wa tahadhari utapigwa kila wanapopaswa kusafiri.
sw.R: Mtakapopiga mlio mkubwa mara ya pili, lazima kambi za upande wa kusini zianze kuondoka. Mlio mkubwa ndio ishara ya kambi kuondoka.

decisions.choice: the camps on the south: Reuben, Simeon and Gad
decisions.reason: Reuben's camp was on the south (2:10-16) and marched second, after the tabernacle had been packed (verses 17-18).

decisions.choice: the Hebrew names only the east and south camps
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives the signals for the first two camps and then states the rule for all. The ancient Greek translation adds a third and a fourth alarm for the camps on the west and north. The Hebrew text is followed here; the other two camps are covered by the general rule at the end of the verse.

decisions.choice: whenever they set out
decisions.reason: The plural "their settings out" makes this the rule for every march, and Balanced says "whenever".

source.text: וּבְהַקְהִ֖יל אֶת־הַקָּהָ֑ל תִּתְקְע֖וּ וְלֹ֥א תָרִֽיעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And when gathering the assembly you will blow, and not will you sound an alarm.

en.L: And when gathering the assembly, you shall blow, but you shall not sound an alarm.
en.B: When you call the assembly together, give a blast on the trumpets, but do not sound the alarm signal.
en.R: To bring the people together, blow the trumpets. Do not use the loud call that tells them to move.

es.L: Y al reunir a la asamblea, {{plural_you:tocarán|tocaréis}}, pero no {{plural_you:tocarán|tocaréis}} alarma.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:convoquen|convoquéis}} a la asamblea, {{plural_you:toquen|tocad}} las trompetas, pero no {{plural_you:den|deis}} el toque de alarma.
es.R: Para reunir al pueblo, {{plural_you:toquen|tocad}} las trompetas. No {{plural_you:usen|uséis}} el toque fuerte que les indica que deben partir.

fr.L: Et pour rassembler l’assemblée, vous sonnerez, mais vous ne sonnerez pas l’alarme.
fr.B: Quand vous convoquerez l’assemblée, sonnez des trompettes, mais ne sonnez pas le signal d’alarme.
fr.R: Pour réunir le peuple, sonnez des trompettes. N’utilisez pas le grand signal qui leur dit de partir.

sw.L: Na wakati wa kulikusanya kusanyiko, mtapiga, lakini hamtapiga mlio wa hatari.
sw.B: Mnapolikusanya kusanyiko, pigeni tarumbeta, lakini msipige mlio wa tahadhari.
sw.R: Ili kuwakusanya watu, pigeni tarumbeta. Msitumie mlio mkubwa unaowaambia waondoke.

decisions.choice: blow ... not sound an alarm: two different signals
decisions.reason: The verse sets the two verbs against each other. The people must not mistake a call to gather for a call to march.

decisions.choice: the assembly: the people gathered as a body
decisions.reason: Here "assembly" is used for the same gathering that verse 2 calls the congregation: the people called together at the tent of meeting (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the loud call that tells them to move
decisions.reason: Readable adds "that tells them to move" to remind the reader what the loud call is used for (verses 5-6).

source.text: וּבְנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים יִתְקְע֖וּ בַּֽחֲצֹצְר֑וֹת וְהָי֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם לְחֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Aaron, the priests, will blow on the trumpets, and they will be for you for a statute of forever for your generations.

en.L: And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow on the trumpets; and they shall be for you a statute forever throughout your generations.
en.B: It is Aaron's sons, the priests, who are to blow the trumpets. Their use is a lasting statute for you, generation after generation.
en.R: Only Aaron's sons, the priests, may blow the trumpets. This law is for you and your descendants for all time.

es.L: Y los hijos de Aarón, los sacerdotes, tocarán las trompetas; y {{plural_you:les serán a ustedes|os serán}} por estatuto perpetuo por {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} generaciones.
es.B: Son los hijos de Aarón, los sacerdotes, quienes tocarán las trompetas. Su uso será para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un estatuto perpetuo, de generación en generación.
es.R: Solo los hijos de Aarón, los sacerdotes, pueden tocar las trompetas. Esta ley es para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} descendientes para siempre.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Aaron, les prêtres, sonneront des trompettes ; et elles seront pour vous une loi perpétuelle pour vos générations.
fr.B: Ce sont les fils d’Aaron, les prêtres, qui sonneront des trompettes. Leur usage sera pour vous une loi perpétuelle, de génération en génération.
fr.R: Seuls les fils d’Aaron, les prêtres, peuvent sonner des trompettes. Cette loi est pour vous et vos descendants, pour toujours.

sw.L: Na wana wa Haruni, makuhani, watapiga tarumbeta; nazo zitakuwa kwenu kanuni ya kudumu milele katika vizazi vyenu.
sw.B: Ni wana wa Haruni, makuhani, watakaopiga tarumbeta. Matumizi yazo yatakuwa kwenu kanuni ya kudumu milele, kizazi hata kizazi.
sw.R: Ni wana wa Haruni tu, makuhani, wanaoruhusiwa kupiga tarumbeta. Sheria hii ni kwa ajili yenu na wazao wenu milele.

decisions.choice: only the priests blow the trumpets
decisions.reason: The trumpets belong to the sanctuary, and blowing them is a priestly duty. Priests blow them again in war (31:6) and in worship (2 Chronicles 5:12; Nehemiah 12:35).

decisions.choice: they will be: the trumpets and their use
decisions.reason: "They" is the trumpets. The rule for them, who blows and when, is a lasting statute.

decisions.choice: a statute forever: a lasting rule for all generations
decisions.reason: "Forever" here means for as long as Israel lives as God's people, through all its generations, as with the other lasting statutes of the law (Exodus 12:14; Leviticus 3:17).

source.text: וְכִֽי־תָבֹ֨אוּ מִלְחָמָ֜ה בְּאַרְצְכֶ֗ם עַל־הַצַּר֙ הַצֹּרֵ֣ר אֶתְכֶ֔ם וַהֲרֵעֹתֶ֖ם בַּחֲצֹצְר֑וֹת וֲנִזְכַּרְתֶּ֗םלִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וְנוֹשַׁעְתֶּ֖ם מֵאֹיְבֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And when you go [to] war in your land against the adversary who attacks you, and you will sound an alarm on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before Yahweh your God, and you will be saved from your enemies.

en.L: And when you go to war in your land against the adversary who attacks you, you shall sound an alarm on the trumpets, and you shall be remembered before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you shall be saved from your enemies.
en.B: In your own land, when you go out to war against an enemy who attacks you, sound the alarm on the trumpets, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will remember you, and you will be saved from your enemies.
en.R: Someday you will be in your own land. When an enemy attacks you there and you go to war, blow the alarm on the trumpets. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will remember you and rescue you from your enemies.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a la guerra en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tierra contra el adversario que {{plural_you:los|os}} ataca, {{plural_you:tocarán|tocaréis}} alarma con las trompetas, y {{plural_you:serán recordados|seréis recordados}} delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios, y {{plural_you:serán salvados|seréis salvados}} de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos.
es.B: En {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} propia tierra, cuando {{plural_you:salgan|salgáis}} a la guerra contra un enemigo que {{plural_you:los|os}} ataque, {{plural_you:toquen|tocad}} alarma con las trompetas, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios se acordará de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:serán librados|seréis librados}} de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos.
es.R: Algún día {{plural_you:estarán|estaréis}} en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} propia tierra. Cuando un enemigo {{plural_you:los|os}} ataque allí y {{plural_you:salgan|salgáis}} a la guerra, {{plural_you:toquen|tocad}} alarma con las trompetas. Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios se acordará de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:los|os}} rescatará de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos.

fr.L: Et quand vous irez à la guerre dans votre pays contre l’adversaire qui vous attaque, vous sonnerez l’alarme avec les trompettes, et vous serez rappelés au souvenir devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu, et vous serez sauvés de vos ennemis.
fr.B: Dans votre propre pays, quand vous partirez en guerre contre un ennemi qui vous attaque, sonnez l’alarme avec les trompettes : {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu se souviendra de vous, et vous serez sauvés de vos ennemis.
fr.R: Un jour, vous serez dans votre propre pays. Quand un ennemi vous y attaquera et que vous partirez en guerre, sonnez l’alarme avec les trompettes. Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu se souviendra de vous et vous délivrera de vos ennemis.

sw.L: Na mtakapokwenda vitani katika nchi yenu dhidi ya adui anayewashambulia, mtapiga mlio wa hatari kwa tarumbeta, nanyi mtakumbukwa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, nanyi mtaokolewa kutoka kwa adui zenu.
sw.B: Katika nchi yenu wenyewe, mtakapotoka kwenda vitani dhidi ya adui anayewashambulia, pigeni mlio wa hatari kwa tarumbeta, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu atawakumbuka, nanyi mtaokolewa kutoka kwa adui zenu.
sw.R: Siku moja mtakuwa katika nchi yenu wenyewe. Adui atakapowashambulia huko nanyi mkaenda vitani, pigeni tarumbeta kwa mlio wa hatari. Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu atawakumbuka na kuwaokoa kutoka kwa adui zenu.

decisions.choice: in your land: looking ahead to life in the promised land
decisions.reason: Israel is still in the wilderness. The statute looks ahead to the time when they live in their own land and must defend it.

decisions.choice: you will be remembered: God will turn to help you
decisions.reason: When God remembers people, he does not merely recall them; he acts for them (Genesis 8:1; Exodus 2:24). The trumpet blast is a cry to God, and God answers by saving his people.

decisions.choice: the alarm on the trumpets: a call to God, not only a call to arms
decisions.reason: The blast calls the army to battle, but the verse ties it to God's remembering and saving. Israel's rescue in war comes from God (31:6; 2 Chronicles 13:12-15).

decisions.choice: the LORD your God will remember you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the passive "you will be remembered before the LORD" into an active sentence with God as subject, which is what the passive means. Literal keeps the passive.

decisions.choice: Someday you will be in your own land.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the look ahead to life in the land a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: "vous serez rappelés au souvenir devant le SEIGNEUR"
alternatives: "on se souviendra de vous devant le SEIGNEUR"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew passive with "devant", as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable make God the subject ("se souviendra de vous").

source.text: וּבְי֨וֹם שִׂמְחַתְכֶ֥ם וּֽבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם֮ וּבְרָאשֵׁ֣י חָדְשֵׁיכֶם֒ וּתְקַעְתֶּ֣ם בַּחֲצֹֽצְרֹ֗ת עַ֚ל עֹלֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְעַ֖ל זִבְחֵ֣י שַׁלְמֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָי֨וּ לָכֶ֤ם לְזִכָּרוֹן֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And on [the] day of your rejoicing and at your appointed feasts and at [the] beginnings of your months, and you will blow on the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over [the] sacrifices of your peace offerings, and they will be for you for a memorial before your God; I [am] Yahweh your God.

en.L: And on the day of your rejoicing, and at your appointed feasts, and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow on the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be for you a memorial before your God. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."
en.B: Also on your days of rejoicing, at your appointed feasts, and on the first day of each month, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your peace offering sacrifices. They will be a reminder of you before your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."
en.R: Also blow the trumpets on your days of celebration, at your special feasts, and on the first day of every month. Blow them when you offer your burnt offerings and your peace offerings. Then the trumpets will remind your God of you. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God."

es.L: Y en el día de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} alegría, y en {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} fiestas señaladas, y en los principios de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} meses, {{plural_you:tocarán|tocaréis}} las trompetas sobre {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} holocaustos y sobre {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} sacrificios de paz; y {{plural_you:les serán a ustedes|os serán}} por memorial delante de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios. Yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios».
es.B: También en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} días de alegría, en {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} fiestas señaladas y el primer día de cada mes, {{plural_you:toquen|tocad}} las trompetas sobre {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} holocaustos y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} sacrificios de paz. Serán un recordatorio de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} delante de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios».
es.R: {{plural_you:Toquen|Tocad}} también las trompetas en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} días de fiesta, en {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} fiestas especiales y el primer día de cada mes. {{plural_you:Tóquenlas|Tocadlas}} cuando {{plural_you:ofrezcan|ofrezcáis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} holocaustos y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} sacrificios de paz. Así las trompetas harán que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios se acuerde de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Dios».

fr.L: Et au jour de votre joie, et à vos fêtes fixées, et aux commencements de vos mois, vous sonnerez des trompettes sur vos holocaustes et sur vos sacrifices de communion ; et elles seront pour vous un mémorial devant votre Dieu. Je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu. »
fr.B: De même, lors de vos jours de réjouissance, de vos fêtes et du premier jour de chaque mois, sonnez des trompettes au-dessus de vos holocaustes et de vos sacrifices de communion. Elles vous rappelleront au souvenir de votre Dieu. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu. »
fr.R: Sonnez aussi des trompettes pendant vos jours de fête, pendant vos grandes fêtes et le premier jour de chaque mois. Sonnez-en quand vous offrez vos holocaustes et vos sacrifices de communion. Ainsi, les trompettes feront penser votre Dieu à vous. Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu. »

sw.L: Na katika siku ya furaha yenu, na katika sikukuu zenu zilizoamriwa, na katika mwanzo wa miezi yenu, mtapiga tarumbeta juu ya sadaka zenu za kuteketezwa na juu ya dhabihu za sadaka zenu za amani; nazo zitakuwa kwenu ukumbusho mbele za Mungu wenu. Mimi [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu."
sw.B: Pia katika siku zenu za furaha, katika sikukuu zenu zilizoamriwa, na siku ya kwanza ya kila mwezi, pigeni tarumbeta juu ya sadaka zenu za kuteketezwa na dhabihu zenu za sadaka za amani. Zitakuwa ukumbusho wenu mbele za Mungu wenu. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu."
sw.R: Pigeni tarumbeta pia katika siku zenu za sherehe, katika sikukuu zenu maalum, na siku ya kwanza ya kila mwezi. Zipigeni mnapotoa sadaka zenu za kuteketezwa na sadaka zenu za amani. Ndipo tarumbeta zitamkumbusha Mungu wenu habari zenu. Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu."

decisions.choice: appointed feasts and beginnings of months: the fixed times of Israel's worship
decisions.reason: The appointed feasts are the yearly festivals set in Leviticus 23. The first day of each month, the new moon, had offerings of its own (28:11-15). "The day of your rejoicing" may be any glad occasion of worship besides these fixed times.

decisions.choice: a memorial before your God: a reminder that brings the people before God
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, being remembered means God turning toward his people with favor. The trumpet sound over the offerings presents the worshipers to God. Compare the stones on the high priest's shoulders, "for a memorial" before the LORD (Exodus 28:12).

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh your God: the seal on the command
decisions.reason: The statement closes the speech, as it closes many laws (Leviticus 18:2, 4). The command rests on who God is and on his bond with his people.

decisions.choice: the trumpets will remind your God of you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the memorial does. It does not mean that God forgets; see m2.

decisions.choice: "les trompettes feront penser votre Dieu à vous"
alternatives: "les trompettes vous rappelleront au souvenir de votre Dieu"
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, the memorial is said plainly as what the sound does: God turns his thought to his people. "Faire penser à" avoids suggesting that God had forgotten them.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֧ה הַשֵּׁנִ֛ית בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֖י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים בַּחֹ֑דֶשׁ נַעֲלָה֙ הֶֽעָנָ֔ן מֵעַ֖ל מִשְׁכַּ֥ן הָעֵדֻֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the year the second, in the month the second, on [the] twentieth in the month, was lifted the cloud from over [the] tabernacle of the testimony.

en.L: And it happened in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth [day] of the month, [that] the cloud was lifted from over the tabernacle of the testimony.
en.B: In the second year, on the twentieth day of the second month, the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle of the testimony.
en.R: In the second year after Israel left Egypt, on the twentieth day of the second month, the cloud rose up from over the tabernacle, the tent that held the covenant tablets.

es.L: Y sucedió en el año segundo, en el mes segundo, a los veinte [días] del mes, [que] la nube se alzó de sobre el tabernáculo del Testimonio.
es.B: En el segundo año, el día veinte del segundo mes, la nube se levantó de encima del tabernáculo del Testimonio.
es.R: En el segundo año después de que Israel salió de Egipto, el día veinte del segundo mes, la nube se elevó de encima del tabernáculo, la tienda que guardaba las tablas del pacto.

fr.L: Et il arriva, la deuxième année, le deuxième mois, le vingtième [jour] du mois, [que] la nuée s’éleva de dessus la Demeure du Témoignage.
fr.B: La deuxième année, le vingtième jour du deuxième mois, la nuée s’éleva et quitta la Demeure du Témoignage.
fr.R: La deuxième année après la sortie d’Égypte, le vingtième jour du deuxième mois, le nuage s’est élevé et a quitté la Demeure, la tente où se trouvaient les tables de l’alliance.

sw.L: Ikawa katika mwaka wa pili, katika mwezi wa pili, [siku ya] ishirini ya mwezi, wingu likainuliwa kutoka juu ya maskani ya Ushuhuda.
sw.B: Katika mwaka wa pili, siku ya ishirini ya mwezi wa pili, wingu liliinuliwa kutoka juu ya maskani ya Ushuhuda.
sw.R: Katika mwaka wa pili tangu Waisraeli walipotoka Misri, siku ya ishirini ya mwezi wa pili, wingu lilipanda juu kutoka kwenye maskani, hema lililokuwa na vibao vya agano.

decisions.choice: the second year, second month, twentieth day: nearly a year after arriving at Sinai
decisions.reason: The years are counted from the exodus (1:1; Exodus 40:17). Israel reached Sinai in the third month of the first year (Exodus 19:1), so they had camped there almost eleven months. The census was ordered nineteen days earlier (1:1), and the second Passover was kept a month before (9:1-5, 11).

decisions.choice: the cloud was lifted: the signal from God to move
decisions.reason: This is the first time the rule of 9:17 is carried out: when the cloud lifted from the tabernacle, the people set out. The departure is God's decision, not Israel's.

decisions.choice: the testimony: the tablets of the covenant kept in the ark
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the two stone tablets with the covenant law, placed in the ark (Exodus 25:16; 31:18). The tabernacle is named from what it holds.

decisions.choice: after Israel left Egypt; the tent that held the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable states the starting point of the year count, and explains "the tabernacle of the testimony" as the terms for this book direct.

source.text: וַיִּסְע֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם מִמִּדְבַּ֣ר סִינָ֑י וַיִּשְׁכֹּ֥ן הֶעָנָ֖ן בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר פָּארָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out [the] sons of Israel by their stages from [the] wilderness of Sinai, and settled the cloud in [the] wilderness of Paran.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel set out by their stages from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set out from the wilderness of Sinai, traveling in stages, and the cloud came to rest in the wilderness of Paran.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} moved out of the wilderness of Sinai, one stage at a time. In the end the cloud stopped in the wilderness of Paran.

es.L: Y partieron los hijos de Israel por sus etapas del desierto del Sinaí, y se asentó la nube en el desierto de Parán.
es.B: Los israelitas partieron del desierto del Sinaí, viajando por etapas, y la nube se posó en el desierto de Parán.
es.R: Los israelitas salieron del desierto del Sinaí, una etapa tras otra. Al final, la nube se detuvo en el desierto de Parán.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël partirent selon leurs étapes du désert du Sinaï, et la nuée demeura dans le désert de Parân.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} partirent du désert du Sinaï, voyageant par étapes, et la nuée vint se poser dans le désert de Parân.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont quitté le désert du Sinaï, une étape après l’autre. À la fin, le nuage s’est arrêté dans le désert de Parân.

sw.L: Na wana wa Israeli wakasafiri kwa safari zao kutoka nyika ya Sinai, na wingu likakaa katika nyika ya Parani.
sw.B: Waisraeli waliondoka katika nyika ya Sinai, wakisafiri hatua kwa hatua, na wingu likatua katika nyika ya Parani.
sw.R: Waisraeli waliondoka katika jangwa la Sinai, kituo kimoja baada ya kingine. Mwishowe wingu likasimama katika jangwa la Parani.

decisions.choice: by their stages: in a series of marches, camp to camp
decisions.reason: The noun is the one used in verse 2 for setting out. The journey went step by step, a march, then a camp, as the cloud led (9:17-23; 33:1-2).

decisions.choice: the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran: a summary of where the journey led
decisions.reason: The verse sums up the whole move from Sinai to Paran. The stops on the way come later in the story (11:3, 34-35), and Israel reaches the wilderness of Paran in 12:16.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Paran: the desert south of Canaan
decisions.reason: Paran is the dry land of the Sinai peninsula's north-east, between Sinai and the southern edge of Canaan. The spies are sent from there (13:3, 26).

decisions.choice: In the end
decisions.reason: Readable marks that the cloud's stop in Paran comes at the end of a journey of several stages (m2).

source.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה עַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out at the first [time] at [the] mouth of Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.

en.L: And they set out for the first time at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the hand of Moses.
en.B: This was the first time they set out at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command, given through Moses.
en.R: This was the first time they moved on as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded through Moses.

es.L: Y partieron por primera vez conforme a la boca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} por mano de Moisés.
es.B: Era la primera vez que partían por orden {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, dada por medio de Moisés.
es.R: Era la primera vez que se ponían en camino como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado por medio de Moisés.

fr.L: Et ils partirent pour la première fois selon la bouche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, par la main de Moïse.
fr.B: C’était la première fois qu’ils partaient sur l’ordre {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, donné par l’intermédiaire de Moïse.
fr.R: C’était la première fois qu’ils se mettaient en route comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait ordonné par Moïse.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kwa mara ya kwanza kwa kinywa cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa mkono wa Musa.
sw.B: Hiyo ilikuwa mara ya kwanza kusafiri kwa amri ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, iliyotolewa kupitia Musa.
sw.R: Hiyo ilikuwa mara ya kwanza kuondoka kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoamuru kupitia Musa.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of Yahweh: at Yahweh's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what is spoken. The same phrase is used for the cloud's signals in 9:18, 20, 23.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means by means of someone. God gave the order, and Moses passed it on.

decisions.choice: at the first: the first march under the new order
decisions.reason: "The first" may mean the first march from Sinai, or the first time the camps moved in the order laid down in chapter 2. Verses 14-28 describe that order, so both come to the same thing here.

source.text: וַיִּסַּ֞ע דֶּ֣גֶל מַחֲנֵ֧ה בְנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֛ה בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֖ה לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם וְעַל־צְבָא֔וֹ נַחְשׁ֖וֹן בֶּן־עַמִּינָדָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out [the] standard of [the] camp of [the] sons of Judah at the first by their armies, and over its army [was] Nahshon son of Amminadab.

en.L: And the standard of the camp of the sons of Judah set out first, by their armies; and over its army [was] Nahshon son of Amminadab.
en.B: The standard of the camp of Judah set out first, division by division, with Nahshon son of Amminadab in command of its forces.
en.R: The tribe of Judah's camp went first, marching by its troops under its flag. Nahshon son of Amminadab was its commander.

es.L: Y partió el estandarte del campamento de los hijos de Judá primero, por sus ejércitos; y sobre su ejército [estaba] Naasón hijo de Aminadab.
es.B: El estandarte del campamento de Judá partió primero, división por división, con Naasón hijo de Aminadab al mando de sus fuerzas.
es.R: El campamento de la tribu de Judá salió primero, marchando por tropas bajo su bandera. Naasón, hijo de Aminadab, era su comandante.

fr.L: Et la bannière du camp des fils de Juda partit en premier, selon leurs armées ; et sur son armée [était] Nahshôn fils d’Amminadab.
fr.B: La bannière du camp de Juda partit la première, division par division, avec Nahshôn fils d’Amminadab à la tête de ses forces.
fr.R: Le camp de la tribu de Juda est parti le premier, en marchant par troupes sous son drapeau. Nahshôn, fils d’Amminadab, en était le commandant.

sw.L: Na bendera ya kambi ya wana wa Yuda ikasafiri kwanza, kwa majeshi yao; na juu ya jeshi lake [alikuwa] Nashoni mwana wa Aminadabu.
sw.B: Bendera ya kambi ya Yuda ilitangulia kusafiri, kikosi kwa kikosi, na Nashoni mwana wa Aminadabu akiwa mkuu wa vikosi vyake.
sw.R: Kambi ya kabila la Yuda ilitangulia, ikitembea kwa vikosi vyake chini ya bendera yake. Nashoni mwana wa Aminadabu alikuwa kamanda wake.

decisions.choice: the standard of the camp: the banner of a camp of three tribes
decisions.reason: Each of the four camps marched under its own standard (2:2). "The standard of the camp of Judah" stands for the whole camp: Judah, Issachar and Zebulun (2:3-9), in the order set in chapter 2.

decisions.choice: armies: the tribe's men organized as fighting units
decisions.reason: The word means a host or army. The men counted in chapter 1 were those able to go out to war (1:3), and the tribes march as an army in its units.

decisions.choice: Nahshon son of Amminadab: the leader of Judah
decisions.reason: He was named as Judah's leader in 1:7 and 2:3, and brought the first offering at the altar's dedication (7:12). The leaders in verses 14-27 are the same as in chapters 1, 2 and 7.

decisions.choice: the camp of Judah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "Judah" for "the sons of Judah", the members of the tribe; Literal keeps "sons". These are the tribe's fighting men, so no inclusive form is used.

decisions.choice: division by division ... its forces (Balanced); its troops ... commander (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use common words for the army's units and its leader. Literal keeps "armies" and "army".

decisions.choice: "des fils de Juda", with no gender span
decisions.reason: These are the tribe's fighting men marching as an army, so, as the English, Literal keeps "fils" with no inclusive alternative (also in verses 15-27).

decisions.choice: "mkuu wa vikosi vyake" (B); "kamanda wake" (R)
decisions.reason: "Kiongozi" is kept for the tribe's leader (nasi'); here the leader is named as the one over the tribe's army, so Balanced says "mkuu" and Readable "kamanda", as the English "in command" and "commander" (also in verses 18, 22, 25).

source.text: וְעַ֨ל־צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י יִשָׂשכָ֑ר נְתַנְאֵ֖ל בֶּן־צוּעָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And over [the] army of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Issachar [was] Nethanel son of Zuar.

en.L: And over the army of the tribe of the sons of Issachar [was] Nethanel son of Zuar.
en.B: Nethanel son of Zuar was over the forces of the tribe of Issachar.
en.R: Nethanel son of Zuar commanded the troops of the tribe of Issachar.

es.L: Y sobre el ejército de la tribu de los hijos de Isacar [estaba] Natanael hijo de Zuar.
es.B: Natanael hijo de Zuar estaba al frente de las fuerzas de la tribu de Isacar.
es.R: Natanael, hijo de Zuar, mandaba las tropas de la tribu de Isacar.

fr.L: Et sur l’armée de la tribu des fils d’Issacar [était] Netanel fils de Tsouar.
fr.B: Netanel fils de Tsouar était à la tête des forces de la tribu d’Issacar.
fr.R: Netanel, fils de Tsouar, commandait les troupes de la tribu d’Issacar.

sw.L: Na juu ya jeshi la kabila la wana wa Isakari [alikuwa] Nethaneli mwana wa Suari.
sw.B: Nethaneli mwana wa Suari alikuwa mkuu wa vikosi vya kabila la Isakari.
sw.R: Nethaneli mwana wa Suari aliongoza vikosi vya kabila la Isakari.

decisions.choice: Issachar marched with Judah, under Judah's standard
decisions.reason: Issachar and Zebulun camped beside Judah on the east (2:5-7) and marched in Judah's camp. Their leaders are those of 1:8-9.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Issachar
decisions.reason: As in verse 14, Balanced and Readable leave out "sons of" before a tribe's name.

source.text: וְעַ֨ל־צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י זְבוּלֻ֑ן אֱלִיאָ֖ב בֶּן־חֵלֽוֹן׃

en.B: Eliab son of Helon was over the forces of the tribe of Zebulun.
en.R: Eliab son of Helon commanded the troops of the tribe of Zebulun.

es.L: Y sobre el ejército de la tribu de los hijos de Zabulón [estaba] Eliab hijo de Helón.
es.B: Eliab hijo de Helón estaba al frente de las fuerzas de la tribu de Zabulón.
es.R: Eliab, hijo de Helón, mandaba las tropas de la tribu de Zabulón.

fr.L: Et sur l’armée de la tribu des fils de Zabulon [était] Éliab fils de Hélon.
fr.B: Éliab fils de Hélon était à la tête des forces de la tribu de Zabulon.
fr.R: Éliab, fils de Hélon, commandait les troupes de la tribu de Zabulon.

sw.B: Eliabu mwana wa Heloni alikuwa mkuu wa vikosi vya kabila la Zabuloni.
sw.R: Eliabu mwana wa Heloni aliongoza vikosi vya kabila la Zabuloni.

decisions.choice: Eliab son of Helon: Zebulun's leader
decisions.reason: As in verse 15. He is named in 1:9, 2:7 and 7:24.

source.text: וְהוּרַ֖ד הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן וְנָסְע֤וּ בְנֵֽי־גֵרְשׁוֹן֙ וּבְנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֔י נֹשְׂאֵ֖י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And was taken down the tabernacle, and set out [the] sons of Gershon and [the] sons of Merari, carriers of the tabernacle.

en.L: And the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who carried the tabernacle, set out.
en.B: Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites set out carrying it.
en.R: Then the tabernacle was taken apart. The families of Gershon and Merari carried it, and they set out next.

es.L: Y fue desmontado el tabernáculo, y partieron los hijos de Gersón y los hijos de Merari, que llevaban el tabernáculo.
es.B: Luego se desmontó el tabernáculo, y partieron los gersonitas y los meraritas, que lo llevaban.
es.R: Después desarmaron el tabernáculo. Las familias de Gersón y de Merari lo cargaron, y salieron a continuación.

fr.L: Et la Demeure fut démontée, et les fils de Guershon et les fils de Merari, qui portaient la Demeure, partirent.
fr.B: Puis la Demeure fut démontée, et les Guershonites et les Merarites partirent en la portant.
fr.R: Ensuite, on a démonté la Demeure. Les familles de Guershon et de Merari l’ont portée, et elles sont parties à leur tour.

sw.L: Na maskani ikashushwa, na wana wa Gershoni na wana wa Merari, waliobeba maskani, wakasafiri.
sw.B: Kisha maskani ilishushwa, na Wagershoni na Wamerari wakasafiri wakiibeba.
sw.R: Kisha maskani ilifunguliwa vipande vipande. Jamaa za Gershoni na Merari ziliibeba, nazo zikaondoka baadaye.

decisions.choice: the Gershonites and Merarites carried the tabernacle's frame and coverings
decisions.reason: These two Levite clans carried the tent's curtains and coverings (Gershon) and its frames, bars, posts and bases (Merari), using the carts given to them (4:24-33; 7:6-8).

decisions.choice: the tabernacle was taken down, and they set out: after Judah's camp, before Reuben's
decisions.reason: The tent was taken down once the first camp had left, and its carriers marched between the first and second camps. This lets them set it up at the next camp before the holy things arrive (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the Gershonites and the Merarites (Balanced); the families of Gershon and Merari (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The sons of Gershon" are the Levite clan descended from him, not his own sons. Literal keeps "sons".

source.text: וְנָסַ֗ע דֶּ֛גֶל מַחֲנֵ֥ה רְאוּבֵ֖ן לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם וְעַל־צְבָא֔וֹ אֱלִיצ֖וּר בֶּן־שְׁדֵיאֽוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out [the] standard of [the] camp of Reuben by their armies, and over its army [was] Elizur son of Shedeur.

en.L: And the standard of the camp of Reuben set out by their armies; and over its army [was] Elizur son of Shedeur.
en.B: Next the standard of the camp of Reuben set out, division by division, with Elizur son of Shedeur in command of its forces.
en.R: The camp of the tribe of Reuben went next, marching by its troops under its flag. Elizur son of Shedeur was its commander.

es.L: Y partió el estandarte del campamento de Rubén por sus ejércitos; y sobre su ejército [estaba] Elisur hijo de Sedeur.
es.B: Después partió el estandarte del campamento de Rubén, división por división, con Elisur hijo de Sedeur al mando de sus fuerzas.
es.R: El campamento de la tribu de Rubén salió después, marchando por tropas bajo su bandera. Elisur, hijo de Sedeur, era su comandante.

fr.L: Et la bannière du camp de Ruben partit selon leurs armées ; et sur son armée [était] Élitsour fils de Shedéour.
fr.B: Ensuite, la bannière du camp de Ruben partit, division par division, avec Élitsour fils de Shedéour à la tête de ses forces.
fr.R: Le camp de la tribu de Ruben est parti ensuite, en marchant par troupes sous son drapeau. Élitsour, fils de Shedéour, en était le commandant.

sw.L: Na bendera ya kambi ya Reubeni ikasafiri kwa majeshi yao; na juu ya jeshi lake [alikuwa] Elisuri mwana wa Shedeuri.
sw.B: Kisha bendera ya kambi ya Reubeni ilisafiri, kikosi kwa kikosi, na Elisuri mwana wa Shedeuri akiwa mkuu wa vikosi vyake.
sw.R: Kambi ya kabila la Reubeni ilifuata, ikitembea kwa vikosi vyake chini ya bendera yake. Elisuri mwana wa Shedeuri alikuwa kamanda wake.

decisions.choice: the camp of Reuben: Reuben, Simeon and Gad
decisions.reason: Reuben's camp, on the south side (2:10-16), was the second to march, as verse 6 says. Its leaders are those of 1:5, 6 and 14.

decisions.choice: Next
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "next" to mark the order of march, which the Hebrew shows by the sequence alone. Readable does the same.

source.text: וְעַ֨ל־צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֑וֹן שְׁלֻֽמִיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־צוּרִֽי שַׁדָּֽי׃

en.B: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the forces of the tribe of Simeon.
en.R: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai commanded the troops of the tribe of Simeon.

es.L: Y sobre el ejército de la tribu de los hijos de Simeón [estaba] Selumiel hijo de Zurisadai.
es.B: Selumiel hijo de Zurisadai estaba al frente de las fuerzas de la tribu de Simeón.
es.R: Selumiel, hijo de Zurisadai, mandaba las tropas de la tribu de Simeón.

fr.L: Et sur l’armée de la tribu des fils de Siméon [était] Shéloumiel fils de Tsourishaddaï.
fr.B: Shéloumiel fils de Tsourishaddaï était à la tête des forces de la tribu de Siméon.
fr.R: Shéloumiel, fils de Tsourishaddaï, commandait les troupes de la tribu de Siméon.

sw.L: Na juu ya jeshi la kabila la wana wa Simeoni [alikuwa] Shelumieli mwana wa Surishadai.
sw.B: Shelumieli mwana wa Surishadai alikuwa mkuu wa vikosi vya kabila la Simeoni.
sw.R: Shelumieli mwana wa Surishadai aliongoza vikosi vya kabila la Simeoni.

decisions.choice: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai: Simeon's leader
decisions.reason: As in 1:6, 2:12 and 7:36. The father's name is written as two words in the Hebrew text here.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Simeon
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

source.text: וְעַל־צְבָ֖א מַטֵּ֣ה בְנֵי־גָ֑ד אֶלְיָסָ֖ף בֶּן־דְּעוּאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And over [the] army of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Gad [was] Eliasaph son of Deuel.

en.L: And over the army of the tribe of the sons of Gad [was] Eliasaph son of Deuel.
en.B: Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the forces of the tribe of Gad.
en.R: Eliasaph son of Deuel commanded the troops of the tribe of Gad.

es.L: Y sobre el ejército de la tribu de los hijos de Gad [estaba] Eliasaf hijo de Deuel.
es.B: Eliasaf hijo de Deuel estaba al frente de las fuerzas de la tribu de Gad.
es.R: Eliasaf, hijo de Deuel, mandaba las tropas de la tribu de Gad.

fr.L: Et sur l’armée de la tribu des fils de Gad [était] Éliasaph fils de Déuel.
fr.B: Éliasaph fils de Déuel était à la tête des forces de la tribu de Gad.
fr.R: Éliasaph, fils de Déuel, commandait les troupes de la tribu de Gad.

sw.L: Na juu ya jeshi la kabila la wana wa Gadi [alikuwa] Eliasafu mwana wa Deueli.
sw.B: Eliasafu mwana wa Deueli alikuwa mkuu wa vikosi vya kabila la Gadi.
sw.R: Eliasafu mwana wa Deueli aliongoza vikosi vya kabila la Gadi.

decisions.choice: Deuel, as in 1:14 and 7:42, 47
decisions.reason: In 2:14 the name is spelled "Reuel" in the Hebrew text. The Hebrew letters for d and r look very much alike and were easily confused in copying. Here the Hebrew has "Deuel", and it is followed.

source.text: וְנָסְעוּ֙ הַקְּהָתִ֔ים נֹשְׂאֵ֖י הַמִּקְדָּ֑שׁ וְהֵקִ֥ימוּ אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן עַד־בֹּאָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And set out the Kohathites, carriers of the holy [things], and they set up the tabernacle until their coming.

en.L: And the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy [things]; and they set up the tabernacle before their arrival.
en.B: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things, and the tabernacle would be standing ready by the time they arrived.
en.R: Then the families of Kohath set out, carrying the holy objects. The other Levites set up the tabernacle before the Kohathites arrived.

es.L: Y partieron los coatitas, que llevaban las [cosas] santas; y levantaban el tabernáculo antes de su llegada.
es.B: Luego partieron los coatitas, llevando los objetos sagrados, y para cuando ellos llegaban el tabernáculo ya estaba levantado.
es.R: Después salieron las familias de Coat, cargando los objetos sagrados. Los otros levitas armaban el tabernáculo antes de que llegaran los coatitas.

fr.L: Et les Kehathites partirent, portant les [objets] saints ; et l’on dressait la Demeure avant leur arrivée.
fr.B: Puis les Kehathites partirent, portant les objets saints, et la Demeure était déjà dressée quand ils arrivaient.
fr.R: Ensuite, les familles de Kehath sont parties, en portant les objets sacrés. Les autres Lévites dressaient la Demeure avant l’arrivée des Kehathites.

sw.L: Na Wakohathi wakasafiri, wakibeba [vitu] vitakatifu; nao wakaisimamisha maskani kabla ya kufika kwao.
sw.B: Kisha Wakohathi walisafiri wakibeba vitu vitakatifu, na maskani ilikuwa imekwisha kusimamishwa walipofika.
sw.R: Kisha jamaa za Kohathi ziliondoka, zikibeba vitu vitakatifu. Walawi wengine waliisimamisha maskani kabla Wakohathi hawajafika.

decisions.choice: the holy things: the sacred objects of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word usually means the sanctuary itself. Here it is what the Kohathites carry: the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars and their utensils, wrapped and carried on poles by hand (3:31; 4:4-15; 7:9).

decisions.choice: they set up the tabernacle before their arrival: the Gershonites and Merarites set it up before the Kohathites came
decisions.reason: "They" who set it up are the carriers of the tent in verse 17, who marched one camp ahead. "Their coming" is the Kohathites' arrival. The tent stood ready to receive the holy things.

decisions.choice: the tabernacle would be standing ready
decisions.reason: Balanced describes the result to avoid an unclear "they"; the meaning is as in m2.

decisions.choice: The other Levites ... the Kohathites
decisions.reason: Readable names both groups so the reader can tell who did what.

decisions.choice: "les Kehathites" (L, B); "les familles de Kehath" (R); "les Guershonites et les Merarites" (verse 17)
decisions.reason: The clan names are formed from the names of Levi's sons as already used (Guershon, Kehath, Merari), so a reader can see the link.

decisions.choice: "Wakohathi" (L, B); "jamaa za Kohathi" (R); "Wagershoni na Wamerari" (verse 17)
decisions.reason: The clans take the Wa- plural of peoples and groups, formed from the names of Levi's sons as already used (Gershoni, Kohathi, Merari).

source.text: וְנָסַ֗ע דֶּ֛גֶל מַחֲנֵ֥ה בְנֵֽי־אֶפְרַ֖יִם לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם וְעַל־צְבָא֔וֹ אֱלִישָׁמָ֖ע בֶּן־עַמִּיהֽוּד׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out [the] standard of [the] camp of [the] sons of Ephraim by their armies, and over its army [was] Elishama son of Ammihud.

en.L: And the standard of the camp of the sons of Ephraim set out by their armies; and over its army [was] Elishama son of Ammihud.
en.B: Next the standard of the camp of Ephraim set out, division by division, with Elishama son of Ammihud in command of its forces.
en.R: The camp of the tribe of Ephraim went next, marching by its troops under its flag. Elishama son of Ammihud was its commander.

es.L: Y partió el estandarte del campamento de los hijos de Efraín por sus ejércitos; y sobre su ejército [estaba] Elisama hijo de Amiud.
es.B: Después partió el estandarte del campamento de Efraín, división por división, con Elisama hijo de Amiud al mando de sus fuerzas.
es.R: El campamento de la tribu de Efraín salió después, marchando por tropas bajo su bandera. Elisama, hijo de Amiud, era su comandante.

fr.L: Et la bannière du camp des fils d’Éphraïm partit selon leurs armées ; et sur son armée [était] Élishama fils d’Ammihoud.
fr.B: Ensuite, la bannière du camp d’Éphraïm partit, division par division, avec Élishama fils d’Ammihoud à la tête de ses forces.
fr.R: Le camp de la tribu d’Éphraïm est parti ensuite, en marchant par troupes sous son drapeau. Élishama, fils d’Ammihoud, en était le commandant.

sw.L: Na bendera ya kambi ya wana wa Efraimu ikasafiri kwa majeshi yao; na juu ya jeshi lake [alikuwa] Elishama mwana wa Amihudi.
sw.B: Kisha bendera ya kambi ya Efraimu ilisafiri, kikosi kwa kikosi, na Elishama mwana wa Amihudi akiwa mkuu wa vikosi vyake.
sw.R: Kambi ya kabila la Efraimu ilifuata, ikitembea kwa vikosi vyake chini ya bendera yake. Elishama mwana wa Amihudi alikuwa kamanda wake.

decisions.choice: the camp of Ephraim: Ephraim, Manasseh and Benjamin
decisions.reason: Ephraim's camp, on the west (2:18-24), was the third to march, after the holy things. Its leaders are those of 1:10-11.

decisions.choice: the camp of Ephraim
decisions.reason: As in verse 14.

source.text: וְעַ֨ל־צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה גַּמְלִיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־פְּדָה־צֽוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And over [the] army of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Manasseh [was] Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

en.L: And over the army of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh [was] Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
en.B: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the forces of the tribe of Manasseh.
en.R: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur commanded the troops of the tribe of Manasseh.

es.L: Y sobre el ejército de la tribu de los hijos de Manasés [estaba] Gamaliel hijo de Pedasur.
es.B: Gamaliel hijo de Pedasur estaba al frente de las fuerzas de la tribu de Manasés.
es.R: Gamaliel, hijo de Pedasur, mandaba las tropas de la tribu de Manasés.

fr.L: Et sur l’armée de la tribu des fils de Manassé [était] Gamaliel fils de Pedahtsour.
fr.B: Gamaliel fils de Pedahtsour était à la tête des forces de la tribu de Manassé.
fr.R: Gamaliel, fils de Pedahtsour, commandait les troupes de la tribu de Manassé.

sw.L: Na juu ya jeshi la kabila la wana wa Manase [alikuwa] Gamalieli mwana wa Pedasuri.
sw.B: Gamalieli mwana wa Pedasuri alikuwa mkuu wa vikosi vya kabila la Manase.
sw.R: Gamalieli mwana wa Pedasuri aliongoza vikosi vya kabila la Manase.

decisions.choice: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur: Manasseh's leader
decisions.reason: As in 1:10, 2:20 and 7:54. The father's name is written as two words joined by a hyphen in the Hebrew text.

es.R: Abidán, hijo de Gedeoni, mandaba las tropas de la tribu de Benjamín.

fr.R: Abidân, fils de Guidéoni, commandait les troupes de la tribu de Benjamin.

sw.B: Abidani mwana wa Gideoni alikuwa mkuu wa vikosi vya kabila la Benyamini.

sw.R: Mwisho kabisa, kambi ya kabila la Dani iliondoka, ikitembea kwa vikosi vyake chini ya bendera yake. Iliulinda upande wa nyuma wa msafara wote. Ahiezeri mwana wa Amishadai alikuwa kamanda wake.

decisions.choice: the rear guard: the one gathering up behind all the camps
decisions.reason: The word means "one who gathers". At the back of the march it names the troops who bring up the rear, protect it and gather any who fall behind (Joshua 6:9, 13; Isaiah 52:12).

decisions.choice: the camp of Dan: Dan, Asher and Naphtali
decisions.reason: Dan's camp, on the north (2:25-31), was the largest after Judah's and marched last, "last by their standards" (2:31). Its leaders are those of 1:12-15.

decisions.choice: Last
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "last", which the rear guard role implies (2:31).

decisions.choice: these were the settings out ... and they set out: the order for every march, followed this time
decisions.reason: "Settings out" is plural: this is the order of march whenever Israel moved. The last verb, "and they set out", tells of the first departure from Sinai (verse 13) and closes the list. The plural also makes it the pattern for later stages.

decisions.choice: the marching order (Balanced); the order in which ... marched (Readable)
decisions.reason: The plural noun means the moves made in this arrangement. Balanced and Readable name the arrangement; Literal keeps "settings out".

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, [the] father-in-law of Moses, setting out [are] we to the place which said Yahweh, it I will give to you; come with us, and we will do good to you, for Yahweh has spoken good concerning Israel.

en.L: And Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, "We are setting out for the place of which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will do you good, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken good concerning Israel."
en.B: Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We are setting out for the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would give us. Come with us and we will be good to you, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has promised Israel good things."
en.R: Moses spoke to Hobab son of Reuel. Hobab's family came from Midian, and they were related to Moses by marriage. Moses said, "We are leaving for the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised to give us. Come with us, and we will be kind to you, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has promised good things for Israel."

es.L: Y dijo Moisés a Hobab hijo de Reuel el madianita, suegro de Moisés: «Nosotros partimos hacia el lugar del cual {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: “{{plural_you:Se lo daré a ustedes|Os lo daré}}”. Ven con nosotros, y te haremos bien, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha anunciado el bien para Israel».
es.B: Moisés dijo a Hobab hijo de Reuel el madianita, suegro de Moisés: «Partimos hacia el lugar que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo que nos daría. Ven con nosotros y te trataremos bien, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha prometido bienes a Israel».
es.R: Moisés habló con Hobab hijo de Reuel. La familia de Hobab era de Madián, y estaba emparentada con Moisés por matrimonio. Moisés le dijo: «Salimos hacia el lugar que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} prometió darnos. Ven con nosotros, y seremos buenos contigo, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha prometido cosas buenas para Israel».

fr.L: Et Moïse dit à Hobab fils de Réuel le Madianite, beau-père de Moïse : « Nous partons vers le lieu dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : “Je vous le donnerai.” Viens avec nous, et nous te ferons du bien, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a annoncé du bien pour Israël. »
fr.B: Moïse dit à Hobab fils de Réuel le Madianite, beau-père de Moïse : « Nous partons pour le lieu dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous le donnerait. Viens avec nous, et nous serons bons pour toi, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a promis du bien à Israël. »
fr.R: Moïse a parlé à Hobab fils de Réuel. La famille de Hobab venait de Madian, et elle était liée à Moïse par mariage. Moïse lui a dit : « Nous partons pour le lieu que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a promis de nous donner. Viens avec nous, et nous te traiterons bien, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a promis de bonnes choses à Israël. »

sw.L: Na Musa akamwambia Hobabu mwana wa Reueli Mmidiani, baba mkwe wa Musa, "Sisi tunasafiri kwenda mahali ambapo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema, 'Nitawapa ninyi mahali hapo.' Njoo pamoja nasi, nasi tutakutendea mema, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenena mema kuhusu Israeli."
sw.B: Musa alimwambia Hobabu mwana wa Reueli Mmidiani, baba mkwe wa Musa, "Tunaondoka kwenda mahali ambapo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema atatupa. Njoo pamoja nasi, nasi tutakutendea wema, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameahidi mambo mema kwa Israeli."
sw.R: Musa alizungumza na Hobabu mwana wa Reueli. Jamaa ya Hobabu ilitoka Midiani, nayo ilikuwa na uhusiano na Musa kwa ndoa. Musa alisema, "Tunaondoka kwenda mahali ambapo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliahidi kutupa. Njoo pamoja nasi, nasi tutakutendea mema, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameahidi mambo mema kwa ajili ya Israeli."

decisions.choice: the father-in-law of Moses: either Reuel or Hobab
decisions.reason: The phrase may describe Reuel, who is Moses' father-in-law in Exodus 2:18-21, or Hobab, who is called Moses' father-in-law in Judges 4:11. Moses' father-in-law is also called Jethro (Exodus 3:1; 18:1). The word may also have had a wider sense, a man related by marriage, which would let Hobab be Moses' brother-in-law. The Hebrew allows either reading, and every level keeps the same order so as not to decide.

decisions.choice: the Midianite: from a desert people who knew the wilderness
decisions.reason: Midian was a people of the desert regions east and south of Canaan. Moses had lived among them as a shepherd for many years (Exodus 2:15; 3:1), and Hobab knew the wilderness well (verse 31).

decisions.choice: we will do good to you ... the LORD has spoken good: a share in God's promised blessing
decisions.reason: The same word "good" ties the two halves together. God has promised good to Israel, the land and its blessings, and Moses offers Hobab a share in that good.

decisions.choice: the place the LORD said he would give us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give God's promise as reported speech, so "you" in the promise becomes "us". Literal keeps the quotation.

decisions.choice: Hobab's family came from Midian, and they were related to Moses by marriage.
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the open question of m1 by saying only that the family was related to Moses by marriage, which is true on either reading.

decisions.choice: "Hobab hijo de Reuel el madianita, suegro de Moisés"
alternatives: "Hobab, suegro de Moisés, hijo de Reuel"
decisions.reason: As in the English, "suegro de Moisés" stays at the end, where it can describe either Reuel or Hobab; the Spanish does not choose between them (see the meaning note).

decisions.choice: "Hobab fils de Réuel le Madianite, beau-père de Moïse"
alternatives: "Hobab, beau-père de Moïse, fils de Réuel"
decisions.reason: As in the English, "beau-père de Moïse" stays at the end, where it can describe either Réuel or Hobab; the French does not choose between them (see the meaning note).

decisions.choice: "Hobabu mwana wa Reueli Mmidiani"
decisions.reason: The name takes the usual Swahili final vowel (Hobabu), and Reueli is the form already used in Genesis and Exodus. "Baba mkwe wa Musa" stays at the end (L, B), where it can describe either man, as in the English.

decisions.choice: my kindred: the family and people I was born into
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to be born". It means one's birthplace and relatives, as when Abram is told to leave his land and his kindred (Genesis 12:1).

decisions.choice: not ... but: a firm refusal
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets "I will not go" against "to my land ... I will go". Hobab means to return home instead.

decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker. Literal and Balanced keep "he".

fr.R: Moïse a dit : « Reste avec nous, s’il te plaît. Tu connais les bons endroits pour camper dans le désert. Tu peux nous montrer le chemin.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Tafadhali usituache, kwa kuwa wewe unajua kupiga kambi kwetu nyikani, nawe utakuwa macho kwa ajili yetu.
sw.B: Musa akasema, "Tafadhali usituache. Wewe unajua mahali tunapoweza kupiga kambi nyikani, nawe utakuwa macho yetu.

decisions.choice: you will be eyes for us: you will be our guide
decisions.reason: To be someone's eyes is to see for them, to guide them where they cannot see the way (compare Job 29:15). Hobab knew the desert, its water and its routes.

decisions.choice: for because thus: since you know
decisions.reason: The joined words give the reason for the request: Hobab's knowledge of the wilderness is why Moses wants him to stay.

decisions.choice: a human guide beside God's guidance
decisions.reason: The cloud and the ark show Israel when to move and where to stop (9:17-23; verses 33-34). Moses still asks for a man who knows the desert. The text does not set the two against each other.

decisions.choice: You can show us the way.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of "eyes" (m1).
