sw.L: Tena itakuwa, ukienda pamoja nasi, mema yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatutendea, sisi tutakutendea wewe."
sw.B: Ukienda pamoja nasi, wema wowote ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatutendea, sisi nasi tutakutendea vivyo hivyo."
sw.R: Ukija pamoja nasi, utapata sehemu ya kila kitu kizuri ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatupa."

decisions.choice: the good which the LORD does for us, we will do for you: a promise to share
decisions.reason: The verse repeats the word "good" three times. Whatever good God gives Israel, Israel will pass on to Hobab.

decisions.choice: if you go with us: the outcome is not told here
decisions.reason: The story does not say whether Hobab went. Later his descendants, the Kenites, are found living among the people of Judah in the land (Judges 1:16; 4:11), which suggests that he or his family did come.

decisions.choice: we will do the same for you (Balanced); you will get a share (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "do the same" for the repeated verb "do good"; Readable puts the promise as a share in the good God gives. Literal keeps the repeated words.

source.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵהַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה דֶּ֖רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וַאֲר֨וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֜ה נֹסֵ֣עַ לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים לָת֥וּר לָהֶ֖ם מְנוּחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from [the] mountain of Yahweh [a] journey of three days, and [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh setting out before them [a] journey of three days to seek out for them [a] resting place.

en.L: And they set out from the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a journey of three days; and the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was setting out before them, a journey of three days, to search out a resting place for them.
en.B: They left the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and marched three days, and all three days the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went ahead of them, searching out a resting place for them.
en.R: The people left the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and walked for three days. The ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the sacred chest, led the way all three days. It went ahead to find a place where they could stop and rest.

es.L: Y partieron del monte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, camino de tres días; y el arca del pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} partía delante de ellos, camino de tres días, para buscarles un lugar de descanso.
es.B: Dejaron el monte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y marcharon tres días, y durante los tres días el arca del pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} fue delante de ellos, buscándoles un lugar de descanso.
es.R: El pueblo dejó el monte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y caminó durante tres días. El arca del pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el cofre sagrado, fue al frente los tres días. Iba adelante para encontrar un lugar donde pudieran parar y descansar.

fr.L: Et ils partirent de la montagne {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, un chemin de trois jours ; et l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} partait devant eux, un chemin de trois jours, pour leur chercher un lieu de repos.
fr.B: Ils quittèrent la montagne {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et marchèrent trois jours ; pendant ces trois jours, l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} alla devant eux pour leur chercher un lieu de repos.
fr.R: Le peuple a quitté la montagne {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et a marché pendant trois jours. L’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le coffre sacré, a ouvert la route pendant ces trois jours. Elle allait devant pour trouver un endroit où ils pourraient s’arrêter et se reposer.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kutoka mlima wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mwendo wa siku tatu; na sanduku la agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likasafiri mbele yao, mwendo wa siku tatu, ili kuwatafutia mahali pa kupumzika.
sw.B: Waliondoka mlima wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wakasafiri siku tatu, na siku zote tatu sanduku la agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} liliwatangulia, likiwatafutia mahali pa kupumzika.
sw.R: Watu waliondoka mlima wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wakatembea siku tatu. Sanduku la agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, lile sanduku takatifu, liliwaongoza siku zote tatu. Lilitangulia mbele kutafuta mahali ambapo wangeweza kusimama na kupumzika.

decisions.choice: the mountain of Yahweh: Mount Sinai
decisions.reason: Sinai, also called Horeb, is "the mountain of God" where God met Moses and gave the covenant (Exodus 3:1; 19:20).

decisions.choice: before them a journey of three days: ahead of them during the three days' march
alternatives: a three days' distance ahead of them
decisions.reason: The phrase "a journey of three days" comes twice. The first time it is the length of the march. The second time it most likely means the same three days, with the ark going ahead of the people. It could also be read as the ark going a three days' distance ahead, which is unlikely, since the people followed it. The repeated phrase may also have been copied twice by mistake.

decisions.choice: the ark went before them: at the head of the march
decisions.reason: In 2:17 and verse 21 the holy things travel in the middle of the camps. Here the ark goes ahead to lead. It may have been carried in front on this first journey, or the verse may speak of the ark as the one who leads, as God goes before his people (Deuteronomy 1:33; Joshua 3:3-6).

decisions.choice: to search out a resting place: to find where they would stop and camp
decisions.reason: The verb is used of scouting land (13:2). The "resting place" is the next campsite, but the word also carries the hope of the rest God promised in the land (Deuteronomy 12:9; Psalm 95:11).

decisions.choice: the sacred chest
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the ark was, as the terms for this book allow, and keeps the word "ark".

decisions.choice: "l'arche ..., le coffre sacré"
decisions.reason: As the English Readable adds "the sacred chest", French keeps "l'arche" and adds "le coffre sacré", since "arche" is otherwise read as Noah's boat or an arch.

decisions.choice: "sanduku ..., lile sanduku takatifu"
decisions.reason: Swahili "sanduku" already means a chest, so the English Readable's added explanation becomes "lile sanduku takatifu" (that holy chest), naming what made it different.

source.text: וַעֲנַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יוֹמָ֑ם בְּנָסְעָ֖ם מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] cloud of Yahweh [was] over them by day, when they set out from the camp.

en.L: And the cloud of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] over them by day, when they set out from the camp.
en.B: By day the cloud of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was above them whenever they moved out from the camp.
en.R: During the day, the cloud of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stayed over them whenever they moved on from their camp.

es.L: Y la nube {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [estaba] sobre ellos de día, cuando partían del campamento.
es.B: De día, la nube {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estaba sobre ellos siempre que salían del campamento.
es.R: Durante el día, la nube {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se quedaba sobre ellos cada vez que dejaban su campamento.

fr.L: Et la nuée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [était] au-dessus d’eux le jour, quand ils partaient du camp.
fr.B: Le jour, la nuée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} était au-dessus d’eux chaque fois qu’ils quittaient le camp.
fr.R: Pendant la journée, le nuage {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} restait au-dessus d’eux chaque fois qu’ils quittaient leur camp.

sw.L: Na wingu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [lilikuwa] juu yao mchana, walipokuwa wakisafiri kutoka kambini.
sw.B: Mchana wingu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilikuwa juu yao kila walipoondoka kambini.
sw.R: Wakati wa mchana, wingu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lilibaki juu yao kila walipoondoka kwenye kambi yao.

decisions.choice: the cloud of Yahweh over them: God's presence covering and guiding
decisions.reason: The cloud that rested on the tabernacle (9:15-16) also went over the people on the march, a sign that God was with them (Exodus 13:21-22; Psalm 105:39).

decisions.choice: when they set out from the camp: whenever they left a campsite
decisions.reason: The form describes what happened each time the people moved on. "The camp" is the place where they had camped.

decisions.choice: the order of verses 34-36
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation places this verse after verses 35-36. The Hebrew order is followed here.

source.text: וַיְהִ֛י בִּנְסֹ֥עַ הָאָרֹ֖ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֑ה קוּמָ֣ה׀יְהוָ֗ה וְיָפֻ֨צוּ֙ אֹֽיְבֶ֔יךָ וְיָנֻ֥סוּ מְשַׂנְאֶ֖יךָ מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when set out the ark, and said Moses, rise up, Yahweh, and let be scattered your enemies, and let flee those hating you from before you.

en.L: And it happened, when the ark set out, that Moses said, \q "Rise up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies be scattered, \q and let those who hate {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} flee from before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, \q "Rise up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies scatter, \q and let those who hate {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} run from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Whenever the ark started out, Moses said, \q "Rise up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! Scatter {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies. \q Make those who hate {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} run away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

es.L: Y sucedió, cuando partía el arca, que Moisés dijo: \q «Levántate, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q y sean esparcidos {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} enemigos, \q y huyan los que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} odian de delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}».
es.B: Cada vez que el arca partía, Moisés decía: \q «¡Levántate, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! \q Que {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} enemigos se dispersen, \q y que los que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} odian huyan de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}».
es.R: Cada vez que el arca se ponía en marcha, Moisés decía: \q «¡Levántate, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! Dispersa a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} enemigos. \q Haz que huyan de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} los que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} odian».

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand l’arche partait, que Moïse dit : \q « Lève-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q et que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} ennemis soient dispersés, \q et que ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} haïssent fuient devant {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} face ! »
fr.B: Chaque fois que l’arche partait, Moïse disait : \q « Lève-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! \q Que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} ennemis se dispersent, \q et que ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} haïssent s’enfuient loin de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ! »
fr.R: Chaque fois que l’arche se mettait en route, Moïse disait : \q « Lève-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Disperse {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} ennemis. \q Fais fuir loin de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} détestent ! »

sw.L: Ikawa, sanduku lilipokuwa likisafiri, Musa alisema, \q "Inuka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q na adui {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} watawanyishwe, \q na wanaokuchukia wakimbie kutoka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}."
sw.B: Kila sanduku lilipoanza safari, Musa alisema, \q "Inuka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Adui {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} na watawanyike, \q na wanaokuchukia wakukimbie."
sw.R: Kila sanduku lilipoanza kwenda, Musa alisema, \q "Inuka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Watawanye adui {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}. \q Wafanye wanaokuchukia wakimbie mbali {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}."

decisions.choice: verses 35-36 are set apart in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew manuscripts these two verses are set off before and after by a special mark, a letter nun written backward. Ancient Jewish tradition treated them as a section of their own. The marks are not words and are not translated.

decisions.choice: when the ark set out, Moses said: what Moses said each time
decisions.reason: The verse describes a custom: the words were said whenever the ark set out, as verse 36 has "he would say" whenever it rested.

decisions.choice: rise up, Yahweh: a call to God to go out as a warrior
decisions.reason: "Rise up" calls God to act, here to go out before his people against their enemies. The ark is the sign of his presence. The saying is taken up in Psalm 68:2 and in Psalm 132:8, where the ark comes to its resting place.

decisions.choice: let {dp('your')} enemies be scattered: a prayer that God's enemies flee
decisions.reason: The verbs express a wish or prayer. The enemies are God's own, "those who hate you": Israel's battles are fought in God's name.

decisions.choice: run from you
decisions.reason: Balanced says "run from" for "flee from before", the sense of the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: Scatter your enemies. Make those who hate you run away
decisions.reason: Readable turns the wishes into requests addressed to God, who is the one who scatters them. The meaning, a prayer that God drive off his enemies, is the same.

decisions.choice: "Levántate" with no span; "{{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}}", "{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}}", "{{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}"
decisions.reason: A clitic joined to the verb takes no span in Spanish, as set for these books; the free pronouns and possessives take it.

decisions.choice: "Lève-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}", "{{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}}", "{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}}"
decisions.reason: French puts the setting on every pronoun addressed to God, including the "toi" joined to the imperative; "ta face" at Literal renders "from before you".

decisions.choice: "adui {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}", "mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}", "mbali {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}"
decisions.reason: Swahili marks "you" inside "wanaokuchukia" and "wakukimbie", where no capital is possible; only the free possessives and "nawe" take the span.

source.text: וּבְנֻחֹ֖ה יֹאמַ֑ר שׁוּבָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה רִֽבְב֖וֹת אַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And when it rested, he would say, return, Yahweh, [to the] ten thousands of [the] thousands of Israel.

en.L: And when it rested, he would say, \q "Return, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q [to] the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel."
en.B: And whenever it came to rest, he would say, \q "Return, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q to Israel's thousands upon thousands."
en.R: When the ark stopped, Moses said, \q "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, come back to the thousands and thousands of Israel."

es.L: Y cuando se detenía, decía: \q «Vuelve, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q [a] las miríadas de los millares de Israel».
es.B: Y cada vez que se detenía, decía: \q «Vuelve, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q a los millares y millares de Israel».
es.R: Cuando el arca se detenía, Moisés decía: \q «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, vuelve con los miles y miles de Israel».

fr.L: Et quand elle se posait, il disait : \q « Reviens, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q [vers] les myriades des milliers d’Israël ! »
fr.B: Et chaque fois qu’elle s’arrêtait, il disait : \q « Reviens, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q auprès des milliers et des milliers d’Israël ! »
fr.R: Quand l’arche s’arrêtait, Moïse disait : \q « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, reviens auprès des milliers et des milliers d’Israël ! »

sw.L: Na lilipotua, alisema, \q "Rudi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q [kwa] makumi ya maelfu ya maelfu ya Israeli."
sw.B: Na kila lilipotua, alisema, \q "Rudi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q kwa maelfu kwa maelfu ya Israeli."
sw.R: Sanduku liliposimama, Musa alisema, \q "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, rudi kwa maelfu na maelfu ya Waisraeli."

decisions.choice: return, Yahweh, to the ten thousands: come back and stay among the people
alternatives: Restore, LORD, the ten thousands of Israel
Return, LORD of the ten thousands of Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no word for "to". The most likely reading is a call for God to return and dwell among his people when the march stops, as "rise up" in verse 35 was a call for him to go out. The verb can also mean "bring back" or "restore", which would make it a prayer for Israel's numbers. Another reading is "Return, Yahweh of the ten thousands".

decisions.choice: the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel: the whole great people
decisions.reason: "Ten thousands" and "thousands" are the largest numbers the language uses, put together to mean a vast multitude. "The thousands of Israel" may also be its divisions (verse 4).

decisions.choice: when it rested: when the ark stopped and was set down
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the "resting place" the ark went to find (verse 33).

decisions.choice: thousands upon thousands (Balanced); thousands and thousands (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the doubled number word as a vast number. Literal keeps the Hebrew words.

decisions.choice: the ark stopped, Moses said
decisions.reason: Readable names the ark and Moses for "it" and "he".

decisions.choice: "las miríadas"
decisions.reason: "Miríada" is ten thousand, used of a vast number, and keeps the two number words of the Hebrew distinct ("miríadas", "millares").

decisions.choice: "les myriades"
decisions.reason: "Myriade" is the French word for ten thousand, used of a vast number, and keeps the two number words of the Hebrew distinct ("myriades", "milliers").
